rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this table pushes obfuscation intensity up while keeping the hot path safe: SUB and SPLIT get high applicability (near-free arithmetic and basic-block splitting, ideal for the small rc4_crypt loop and rc4_setup KSA where every instruction matters at 1148 bytes of text); BCF keeps high SecurityGain but its honest high RuntimeCost/SizeCost lets the selector suppress it in the hot RC4 keystream loop while still applying it to cold main and _start; FLA is rated moderately useful with elevated CorrectnessRisk (0.55) so it only triggers on control-flow-dense functions like the KSA, not the tight crypt loop; IBR and ICALL get solid security/diversity with moderate costs since bogus control flow and indirect calls add real analysis friction cheaply at this binary size; IGV carries the highest DiversityGain (0.80) with low SizeCost because global variable remapping compounds well with SUB and costs almost nothing in a 4-function binary, with a moderate CorrectnessRisk penalty to avoid it on pointer-heavy code.
